children: New York Fed President John Williams expects one more interest hike will be appropriate late this year if the economy evolves broadly in line with his forecast, he said Tuesday.
After the Federal Open Market Committee
by 25 basis points at its September meeting, he is in no rush for another rate hike in October. "There is no need for urgency, and we have time to gather more information," Williams said.

"The accumulation of more data should provide greater clarity on the underlying trends in the economy and the associated risks to achieving our goals — and thereby the appropriate setting of monetary policy," he said.
He'll remain open to how the data unfolds. "That is just my forecast, and time —and the totality of the data — will tell," Williams said.

Regarding the current economic picture, the risk to maximum employment has receded and the risk to achieving price stability has increased, he noted. Specifically, he pointed out that "the inflationary impact of the AI-related demand shock is increasingly salient, and I now expect somewhat larger and longer-lasting effects from energy prices on inflation."

Williams expects real GDP growth to average 2 1/4% this and next year, slightly above its longer-run trend pace. Due to the economic momentum, he expects unemployment to tick down to ~4% over the next year. For inflation, he expects inflation to be at ~3.5% this year, then move to just above 2% next year and reach the Fed's longer-run inflation goal of 2% in 2028.

"It is imperative that we return inflation to our 2% target on a sustained basis," he emphasized. "To do so, we must make certain that adverse inflationary disturbances do not become entrenched and that any second-round effects on inflation remain muted."

In other words, while monetary policy policy can't resolve supply shocks, such as moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz, "it can diminish the risk that these supply shocks spill over into broader and more persistent inflation," he said.

title: New York Fed's Williams sees one more rate hike late this year
